title.ko: 문체 전환: 격식–중립–구어 · request · refuse · greet · 이메일 vs 문자
title.en: register shifting: formal, neutral, colloquial; requests, refusals, greetings; email vs text

explain.ko: 문체(register)는 상황, 상대, 매체에 따라 달라지는 언어의 격식 수준입니다. 격식체는 길고 정중한 구조와 완전한 문장(Would you be so kind as to ...)을, 중립체는 보통의 표현(Could you ...?)을, 구어체는 줄임말과 속어(Can you ...?)를 씁니다. 이메일과 문자, 보고서와 대화의 차이처럼 같은 내용이라도 문체에 따라 인상이 크게 달라지므로, 상대와 맥락에 맞게 의식적으로 선택해야 합니다.
explain.en: Register is the level of formality of language that varies with situation, listener and medium. A formal register uses long polite structures and complete sentences (Would you be so kind as to ...), a neutral register uses ordinary expressions (Could you ...?), and a colloquial register uses contractions and slang (Can you ...?). As with emails versus texts, or reports versus speech, the same content gives a very different impression in different registers, so choose consciously to suit the person and context.

lines.t: Formality has levels. A formal register uses long, polite sentences, a neutral register uses ordinary expressions, and a colloquial register uses contractions and slang. The same content leaves a very different impression depending on tone, so choose to suit the person and situation.

items.passage:
WRITING GUIDE
Choosing a register
In formal writing, avoid contractions and slang and write complete sentences. In writing to friends, a relaxed tone is natural. Practising the same content in two registers helps.

trans.ko:

문체 선택
격식 있는 글에서는 줄임말과 속어를 피하고, 문장은 완전하게 쓰세요. 반면 친구에게 보내는 글은 편안한 어조가 자연스럽습니다. 같은 내용을 두 가지 문체로 써 보는 연습이 도움이 됩니다.

prompt.en: Write the same request in formal, neutral and colloquial registers (three sentences plus one explanatory sentence).

task.model: Formal: Would you be so kind as to reschedule the meeting? Neutral: Could you change the meeting time? Colloquial: Can you shift the meeting? Choose your register to suit the person and situation.
